about: One fictional Series A, as the documents that carry it: a term sheet in two versions, the subscription and shareholders' agreement, the articles of association, the option scheme rules and the cap table they produce. Every clause is a node; every link between clauses is an edge. The company, the people and the numbers are invented. UK practice, simplified.
caveats: Fictional. Example Robotics Ltd, its founders and its investors do not exist, and the numbers are chosen to make the arithmetic easy to follow.
Not legal advice. The clauses are short summaries of what such clauses usually do, written for this example, not drafting to copy. Real documents are longer and the detail matters.
UK practice, simplified. Clause names and structure follow common English practice for venture rounds; other jurisdictions put the same rights in different documents.
The cap table assumes every option in the pool is granted and exercised, ignores exercise prices and tax, and treats seed shares as ordinary shares.

versions.note: First draft, sent by the lead investor.
Agreed draft, after the founders' reply.

documents.title: Series A term sheet
documents.summary: The short document both sides negotiate first. Almost all of it is not binding; it is the map the long-form documents are drafted from.

clauses.title: Investment and valuation
clauses.text: The investors subscribe £3,000,000 for Series A preferred shares at a pre-money valuation of £12,000,000, on a fully diluted basis that includes the new option pool.
clauses.caveat: "Fully diluted" and "pre-money" together mean the new option pool is paid for by the existing shareholders, not the new investor. Read it with the option pool clause.

clauses.title: Option pool

text.v1: Before completion the company creates an unallocated option pool equal to 10% of the fully diluted share capital after completion, counted in the pre-money valuation.
text.v2: Before completion the company creates an unallocated option pool equal to 8% of the fully diluted share capital after completion, counted in the pre-money valuation.

clauses.change: The founders showed a two-year hiring plan that uses 8%. The pool was cut to what the plan needs, which moves part of the company back to the existing shareholders; the cap table computes how much.
clauses.caveat: The size of the pool is a valuation term in disguise: every point of pool in the pre-money valuation lowers the price per share.

clauses.title: Liquidation preference

text.v1: On a sale or winding up, Series A holders first receive their investment back (1x), and then share in what remains with the ordinary shares, pro rata (participating).
text.v2: On a sale or winding up, Series A holders receive the greater of their investment back (1x) or what they would receive as ordinary shares (non-participating).

clauses.change: Moved from participating to non-participating. On a mid-sized exit this is the clause that moves the most money; the waterfall shows how much.
clauses.caveat: A 1x non-participating preference is a common position at Series A; participation, multiples above 1x and cumulative dividends each move value from founders to investors on smaller exits.

clauses.title: Anti-dilution
clauses.text: If the company later issues shares at a lower price, Series A holders are protected on a broad-based weighted average basis, with the usual exceptions such as the option pool.
clauses.caveat: Broad-based weighted average is the milder form. Full ratchet, which reprices the whole investment to the new lower price, is rare and expensive for founders.

clauses.title: Board
clauses.text: A board of four: the two founders, one director appointed by the investors, and one independent director agreed by both.
clauses.caveat: Control rarely moves through the board count alone; read it with the consent matters, which can matter more.

clauses.title: Investor consent matters
clauses.text: An investor majority must consent before the company issues new shares, changes its business, sells itself, borrows above an agreed limit or adopts its annual budget.
clauses.caveat: This list is where control actually sits. A long list here can matter more than a board seat.

clauses.title: Pre-emption
clauses.text: Existing shareholders may take up new shares before they are offered to anyone else, pro rata to their holdings.
clauses.caveat: Pre-emption protects against dilution only for holders with money to follow on; angels often cannot.

clauses.title: Drag-along and tag-along
clauses.text: If the board, an investor majority and a majority of shareholders approve a sale, everyone must sell on the same terms (drag). If a controlling stake is sold, every holder may sell on the same terms (tag).
clauses.caveat: Who can trigger the drag decides who can sell the company. Check whose approval it needs.

clauses.title: Founder vesting

text.v1: Founder shares vest back over four years from completion, with a one-year cliff. Good leaver and bad leaver terms apply.
text.v2: Founder shares vest back over three years from completion, with 25% treated as vested at completion for time already served and no cliff. Good leaver and bad leaver terms apply.

clauses.change: The founders had worked on the company for two years before the round. The reply asked for that time to count; the agreed draft credits a quarter of it and drops the cliff.
clauses.caveat: Reverse vesting on shares the founders already own is the investor's protection against a founder leaving early. The leaver definitions decide what it costs.

clauses.title: Information rights
clauses.text: Monthly management accounts, the annual budget before the year starts, and audited accounts within 120 days of the year end.
clauses.caveat: Cheap to agree and expensive to keep up without a finance function; this is where a deal room as a vault would carry its weight.

clauses.title: What is binding

text.v1: This term sheet is not legally binding, except for confidentiality, eight weeks' exclusivity, and the company paying the investors' legal costs up to £40,000.
text.v2: This term sheet is not legally binding, except for confidentiality, six weeks' exclusivity, and the company paying the investors' legal costs up to £30,000.

clauses.change: Exclusivity shortened by two weeks and the cost cap lowered by £10,000.
clauses.caveat: These are the only clauses with force before the long-form documents are signed. Exclusivity stops the company talking to other investors while the clock runs.

documents.title: Subscription and shareholders' agreement
documents.summary: The contract between the company, the founders and the investors: who pays what, what the founders promise, and how the company is run.

clauses.title: Subscription and completion
clauses.text: The investors subscribe for the Series A shares at the price per share the valuation sets; the company issues them and updates its register at completion.

clauses.title: Warranties and disclosure
clauses.text: The company and the founders give warranties about the business, qualified by a disclosure letter. Claims are capped and time-limited.
clauses.caveat: Not in the term sheet at all, and often where most of the legal time goes. The disclosure letter is the founders' protection: what is disclosed cannot later be claimed for.

clauses.title: Board and observers
clauses.text: Sets the board of four, the investor director's appointment and removal, and an observer seat.

clauses.title: Investor consents
clauses.text: Lists the matters that need investor majority consent, in a schedule.

clauses.title: Founder restrictive covenants
clauses.text: Founders agree not to compete or solicit staff and customers for a period after they leave.
clauses.caveat: Courts look at whether such restrictions are reasonable in length and scope; ask what is usual before agreeing.

clauses.title: Information
clauses.text: The reporting the term sheet promised, with the dates and who receives it.

documents.title: Articles of association
documents.summary: The company's constitution, filed at Companies House. The rights that attach to each class of share live here, so they bind every future holder.

clauses.title: Share classes and rights
clauses.text: Creates the Series A preferred shares and sets the rights of each class: votes, dividends, conversion to ordinary shares.

clauses.title: Return of capital and exit
clauses.text: Sets the order in which proceeds are paid out on a sale or winding up: the liquidation preference, written as a waterfall.

clauses.title: Anti-dilution
clauses.text: The weighted average formula, and the issues it excludes.

clauses.title: Pre-emption on issue
clauses.text: Existing holders' right to take up new shares first, and the issues it does not cover.

clauses.title: Leavers and compulsory transfer
clauses.text: When a founder leaves, unvested shares must be offered back: at fair value for a good leaver, at the lower of cost and fair value for a bad leaver.
clauses.caveat: The definition of "bad leaver" is the clause to read twice. Some drafts include resignation for any reason.

clauses.title: Drag-along
clauses.text: The approval thresholds that force every holder to sell, and the terms they must be offered.

clauses.title: Tag-along
clauses.text: Any holder may join a sale of a controlling stake on the same terms.

documents.title: Option scheme rules
documents.summary: How the pool is granted to employees. In the UK, EMI options are often used where the company qualifies.

clauses.title: Pool size and grants
clauses.text: The board may grant options over the shares reserved in the pool, with vesting set per grant.
clauses.caveat: Whether a company qualifies for EMI depends on conditions set by HMRC; check before promising EMI options to new hires.

clauses.title: Leavers
clauses.text: What happens to vested and unvested options when an employee leaves.

documents.title: Cap table
documents.summary: Not a contract but what the contracts produce. Computed by the build from the round terms, so each version of the term sheet has its own cap table.

clauses.title: The round
clauses.text: Price per share and new shares, computed from the investment and the pre-money valuation.

clauses.title: The pool
clauses.text: The new pool, sized so that it is the agreed share of the company after completion.

clauses.title: The exit waterfall
clauses.text: Who receives what at a range of exit values, under each version's preference.
